patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Clay and Gong share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Clay only if your buying job matches “GTM data enrichment and workflow platform for multi-provider waterfall prospecting — Free ” rather than Gong's shape. Choose Gong only if your buying job matches “Conversation intelligence / revenue AI — per-user licenses + platform fee; custom proposal” rather than Clay's shape. Workflow advantage: Clay leans data-enrichment, prospecting; Gong leans sales-engagement. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Clay and Gong share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Clay is GTM data enrichment and workflow platform for multi-provider waterfall prospecting — Free + Launch from ~$167/mo headline, Growth, Enterpris; Gong is Conversation intelligence / revenue AI — per-user licenses + platform fee; custom proposal only (no public dollar list)..
- Company-size focus: Clay (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Gong (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Clay-leaning data-enrichment, prospecting vs Gong-leaning sales-engagement.
- Researched limits: Clay — Learning curve is steep for non-technical GTM users — table/waterfall mental model; Gong — Separate job from sales intelligence contact databases.

Limitations — Clay: Learning curve is steep for non-technical GTM users — table/waterfall mental model; Credit consumption across providers requires ongoing cost governance; Gong: Separate job from sales intelligence contact databases; Not a prospecting/enrichment data core.

Poor-fit cases: Clay is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Learning curve is steep for non-technical GTM users — table/waterfall mental model · Gong is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Separate job from sales intelligence contact databases · Avoid Clay if you actually need Gong's motion (Conversation intelligence / revenue AI — per-user licenses + platform fee; custo)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
